:::{#def-quotient}

#### Quotient

For real numbers $a$ and $b$ with $b \neq 0$,
the **quotient** of $a$ by $b$
is the result of dividing $a$ by $b$:

$$\frac{a}{b}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-fraction}
#### Fraction, numerator, and denominator

A quotient $\frac{a}{b}$ (@def-quotient) is also called a **fraction**;
$a$ is its **numerator** and $b$ its **denominator**.
For example, the fraction $\frac{6}{4}$ has numerator $6$ and denominator $4$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-quotient}
#### A quotient

The quotient of $6$ by $4$ is $\frac{6}{4} = 1.5$.
The quotient of $6$ by $0$ is undefined,
because @def-quotient requires a nonzero denominator.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-rate}
#### Rate

A **rate** is a quotient whose denominator measures time,
such as weeks or person-years of follow-up.
For example, $12$ new cases in $4$ weeks
is a rate of $\frac{12}{4} = 3$ new cases per week,
and $30$ cases over $10{,}000$ person-years of follow-up
is a rate of $\frac{30}{10{,}000} = 0.003$ cases per person-year.

:::

::: notes
cf. <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rate_(mathematics)>
:::
